The five-case source-based desk evaluation now covers physics plus simulation, mathematics plus proof, Rule 30 cellular automata, empirical taxonomy with observations, and cross-formalism translation. It distinguishes documented core coverage from partial support, composition requirements, and out-of-scope areas, with explicit synthetic test fixtures and expected outputs. The evidence favors a compositional approach: DOL/MMT/institution theory for formal integration; Modelica/FMI or SysML v2/KerML for selected executable models; SKOS/OWL, SOSA/SSN, and PROV-O for taxonomy, observations, and provenance; and OAEI for ontology-matching evaluation. No universal MECE factorization has been established. Tool-level tests remain outstanding, so novelty is not yet demonstrated. Before merging, full schema and relation-signature validation is being applied to the graph; the candidate frameworks have not been executed in their tools.

The fixture oracles have now been independently checked: a standalone Python RK4 integration of the harmonic oscillator matched analytic positions and velocities at t = 0, π/2, π with maximum absolute error about 2.081e-13; the computed Rule 30 trace matched all six expected rows and the all-zero state was confirmed as a fixed point; bounded checks of n+0=n for n=0..1000 and the toy age-field mapping passed. Separately, the existing FOL Operational Metamodel workspace passed 21 Python unit tests covering import of a pinned compiled MMT FOL OMDoc artifact, finite-structure formula satisfaction, sort/arity rejection, and the distinction between truth in one structure and semantic consequence. These checks validate the fixture oracles and adjacent local code, not the candidate frameworks themselves; DOL/MMT/SysML/Modelica runtimes have not been run against the five fixtures. Next: extend the existing formal-logic prototype with one checkable theorem and one explicit translation/preservation test, then run a dynamic model in a suitable Modelica/FMI or SysML environment.

The toy mapping case was strengthened from a superficial sanity check to an actual bounded mapping: I generated 1,001 Person records with nonnegative integer ages, mapped each record to Human.ageYears, and verified every mapped age matched its source and remained a nonnegative integer. A negative control that copied an age-in-days value directly into ageYears was detected as invalid. This remains a bounded hand-coded test, not a proof of general semantic preservation or a test of DOL/MMT/SysML/Modelica.

It returned UNSAT for the counterexample query n >= 0 AND n + 0 != n and emitted an internal proof object. It returned UNSAT for the identity-age mapping postcondition and the exact integer days-to-years conversion query, and SAT with model years=1, days=365 for a negative control that copies days into years. These are solver-level checks of explicit formulas, not MMT/DOL conformance or independently kernel-checked proof-assistant results.
